flashcards.term: Describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for Activity 12.3 (To map biotic and abiotic components in a school garden ecosystem.).
flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for activity 12.3 (to map biotic and abiotic components in a school garden ecosystem.).]
flashcards.definition:
Aim: To map biotic and abiotic components in a school garden ecosystem.
Materials: Field notebook, Magnifying glass, Thermometer
Steps: Select a 2m x 2m quadrant in a school garden. List biotic elements (plants, insects, worms, birds). List abiotic elements (soil moisture, sunlight, air temp). Draw a food chain connecting species.
Observation: Plants act as producers eaten by caterpillars (consumers), decomposed by soil fungi.
Principle: Interdependence between living and non-living components sustains ecosystem health.

flashcards.term: Detail the role of producers, consumers, and decomposers in maintaining ecological balance.
flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: detail the role of producers, consumers, and decomposers in maintaining ecological balance.]
flashcards.definition: 1. Producers (Autotrophs): Capture solar energy to synthesize organic food via photosynthesis, forming the base of all food chains. 2. Consumers (Heterotrophs): Transfer energy across trophic levels (herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat herbivores), controlling population densities. 3. Decomposers (Saprotrophs): Break down complex organic waste into simple inorganic nutrients, returning minerals to soil for plant reabsorption.
